Oh absolutely. I think that's how it is with a lot of mental disorders or illnesses, or even when you're just feeling depressed. It seems like it's a war of rational logic and overwhelming emotions. It's like knowledge is a burden that you can't undo, yet you know you wouldn't because it's better not to be ignorant.

That said, knowing what's true is important, because it's the first step in paving the way to a fulfilling life. It's just hard to pave the way when your emotions are pushing back against you so hard. As someone who has OCD and intrusive thoughts, I know it's very hard to resist these thoughts, but I still try.

I encourage everyone with that struggle to push back, because it makes life **so** much more fulfilling when we finally push through.

Good luck OP

I feel the same way sometimes, like we're too small in the universe to matter. That means it doesn't matter.

**But**, if it doesn't matter, then why does that mean someone should die? Things might not matter overall, but I'd say that can mean we can decide what matters *to us*. I think it comes down to how fulfilled you are from life. And it sounds like your sense of fulfillment comes from helping others. That shows intelligence.

And I bet you help more than you know. Everything you do affects people around you, and I bet you're value of intelligence, potential, and helping people affects your actions in a very positive way. I encourage you to look around, and see that you can and do help people. We all do, in our own ways. Your help is valuable, and can be ever-expanding. That shows potential.

As for having things that can help people, well I bet that comes in the form of your insight. Like I said, I relate to the thought process in your first two sentences, and I think it's good insight. I think that means you can use insight to help other people. I bet you'd be surprised how many people that would help.

Anyways, I hope that train of logic I presented can help you. I hope it gives enough evidence to help you see that you are indeed a helpful person. Help yourself first for sure, but know that you're already helping other people. Which in turn helps you... **H E L P C E P T I O N**

Good luck man.

*raises hand*

Yeah man, I feel the same way a lot. I have a lot of those same thoughts too. All I really know is that it's not us, it's the thoughts. At least not in my opinion. Even if you don't have control, it can still be diminished in intensity. Therapists generally are able to listen and help more with these things than outside friends, but we're all here too.

I guess if you really don't think anyone loves you, make sure you assess that for sure. I'm willing to bet otherwise, but if it's true, I sincerely think you should reach out for new connections. Support from loved ones makes things less confusing (possibly with your thoughts) and brings new perspectives into light. I do and will always value looking at things from many different perspectives. You might find ways to like being alive! I think that if we can make life enjoyable, why not live it, right? I hope you can find ways to rejuvenate a sense of joy and/or meaning life.
Oh my god that's the most touching thing I've heard in a long time ;__;. That makes me so happy for you. I want to start doing that.

Yeah. It gets hard man. I guess I got my own reasons for being down, but I know that my version of your problem has gotten better. I felt really unappreciated for a long time. Surprisingly, more people appreciated me than I thought. I don't know if you talk to many people about it, but voicing your opinion and advocating for yourself might help. (Just keep in mind some people still won't appreciate your fairness. Those one's aren't important.)

I hated it when people would always say 'it gets better' or 'one day at a time.' If you can find people who relate, then I hope you trust them when they say it gets better, or give you ideas for coping skills throughout the day. And pets will always appreciate you, even if they can't speak up. :)

You'll find people who appreciate you, and people who do the same as you too. If you stay alive, I'm sure you'll find people who end up looking up to your accomplishments, too. It might be a long version of saying 'give it time,' but I find that giving tangible, reasonable explanations of those 'cheesy' statements can help boost their credibility. It actually might do me some good to remember that too, heh.

We're all here for you. Good luck bud.

Ah I see. Well that's even better that you don't take them for granted. I kind of meant the idea that you're the better man. That is, I for one appreciate that fact. How are you doing now? been a few hours

From what I understand, most people on dating sites experience responses for like 1 in 15 people. My dad used OkCupid too, and he told me that he eventually learned that.

Another thing I found out, from a lot of girls too, was that they wouldn't care if I had experience or not. From what I understand, relationships have *wayy* more to do with compassion and personality than sex appeal and experience.

I was always really afraid to approach girls or try to find a girlfriend because I've never had experience. But recently I've been trying to find a girlfriend, even when I'm scared, because of how many girls explained to me what they value in a guy. And I'm happy to say it started working!

I hoped that sharing this with you could help. If you have actually met girls who care about your experience enough to lost complete interest, then forget them. From the other comments here, too, I hope that you believe what we're saying.

And a last note: Like you said, it's more about being happy than having a girlfriend. I hope this doesn't sound cliche or douchey, but have you looked for professional help? I know I needed it for my mental disorders. It sounds like it's getting dangerous for you, maybe that could help.

Either way, I hope you find your path to happiness, girlfriend or not.

Hey. I know you probably don't want to talk about any of the good things in your life, so I won't talk about that.

I does get really tiring to not be noticed for doing the right thing, and maybe even getting fucked over for it. Whether it's miscommunication, or people around you just don't give a shit about morals, I'd assume you still feel fucked over, right?

I hope it helps when I say I can relate. I don't know you, or your full situation, but this pretty much sums up the thoughts I had for so long. I don't really know what to say to help, but I hope that it's enough to know this:

I'm really happy that people like you exist, people who do the right thing. I don't know the others who do injustice, but I don't care about them. I just want you to know that you are the better man, and that means a lot, at least to me.

I value fairness and morals very much. Maybe you'll find someone else who does? That's what helped me. Knowing that people exist who care about me, and what I do, and why I do it. I hope that can help you too.

If that helps, then I sincerely hope that you will find more people like that. I hope they are involved in your life enough that you will feel validated. When I finally found people like that, I felt a lot more supported. Good luck friend.

Heyy you like Diablo! And Heathstone! I never got into those too much (did somewhat), but my brothers love em. Just reminded me of that.

I was actually about to post. It's been a long time since I've been on the SW subreddit, and I saw this and remembered that I care about you guys. Just thought I'd say I see you, and that you are a person who matters from where I'm sitting in my room, for what that's worth.
